app.title: Mic Console
mute.title: The mic is sending pure digital silence. Press the mute button on the mic itself.
q.title: Second virtual mic: “{name}”. Select it in an app to get heavier AI noise removal; audio arrives {delay} late. Use it for recordings, voice messages and streams; stick to the regular mic for live calls.
q.title.locked: The model can't start right now (GPU memory or model file); the mic keeps working with regular processing.
stale.text: The panel has been updated; this tab is showing an old version.
err.auth: missing or expired key — run `mic console` in a terminal and open the URL it prints
err.noauth: This browser isn't authorized yet. Run `mic console --open` in a terminal to open the panel with access. (For security, the panel only works with your key.)
msg.nomic: Mic not detected: check the USB cable.
msg.nochain: The processing chain isn't running: systemctl --user start mic-clean.service
char.hint: Shapes the tone of your voice and stays put when you change modes. Sits after the noise gate and before the limiter.
live.hint: Turn it on, talk, and switch characters to hear the change in your headphones right away.
live.hint.on: Talk and switch characters; you'll hear the difference right away (about a quarter second late over Bluetooth).
char.pitchnote: Lower and Bigger shift your pitch: switching to or away from them restarts the mic for 2–3 seconds and adds about 60 ms of latency. In Whisper, Night and Raw modes only their EQ part applies.
amt.label: Intensity
charsave.hint: You've tweaked it by hand. Save this tone under a name:
chardel.hint: One of your own characters is selected.
pitch.hint: Shifts your voice lower or higher. Toggling it restarts the mic for a few seconds; while on, it adds about 60 ms of latency. Pitch shifting doesn't work on whispers, so it's bypassed automatically in Whisper, Night and Raw modes.
pitch.formant.hint: On: still you, just lower or higher. Off: the vocal tract shifts too, so shifting down sounds like a bigger person and shifting up like a smaller one.
deess.hint: Tames harsh “s” and “sh” sounds by turning down only the top end, leaving the body of your voice alone. It also dulls whispers a little, so it switches off automatically in Whisper, Night and Raw modes.
body.hint: Keeps your low end steady and full: holds on to body that fades on soft syllables without bloating loud ones. Try it with Deep or Warm. Whispers have almost no low end, so it would only raise rumble; it switches off automatically in Whisper, Night and Raw modes.
mud.hint: Turn on if your low end gets boomy and muddy when you lean in or on heavy syllables. A dynamic EQ that dips the low mids only when they swell; calm speech is left untouched.
harsh.hint: Turn on if loud syllables sound piercing. A dynamic EQ that dips the upper mids only in those moments. It also dulls whispers, so it switches off automatically in Whisper, Night and Raw modes.
aud.hint: Live monitoring gets muddied by your own voice in the room and Bluetooth latency. Here you record one take and play the same take back through each character. Playback never changes your settings.
aud.label: Play the take — pick a character:
aud.measure.hint: Shows how your take stacks up against broadcast loudness specs.
dv.clicks.b: . Keyboard noise counts too; not calibrated yet
aud.note: The take is kept only in this computer's temporary memory and is deleted when you record a new one, after 15 minutes unused, or when the panel shuts down. The character is bypassed for a few seconds while recording.
meter.note_html: While you talk, the Output bar should stay inside the shaded zone. If the Mic bar turns red, turn the gain knob on the mic down a little: the signal is clipping inside the mic, and software can't undo that.
gain.same: The chain is currently leaving your level unchanged.
gain.up: The chain is currently adding {db} dB of gain.
gain.down: The chain is currently pulling your level down by {db} dB.
hpf.a: Cuts mains hum and desk rumble (below
hpf.b: Hz). Most of the mic's low-frequency noise goes here.
auto.p: Rides your level toward the target automatically: lifts whispers, pulls loud speech down. It freezes the gain when you stop talking, so background noise doesn't creep up.
auto.hint: If your whisper isn't being lifted, lower the silence threshold; if noise rises when you stop talking, raise it.
comp.p: Smooths out sudden loud syllables. Kept gentle (3:1); the leveler handles the big level swings.
ns.p: Removes hiss and steady background noise (AI model). Leaves whispers intact. The most CPU-hungry stage when on.
gate.p: Turns down what's left when you stop talking: breaths between phrases, keyboard, clicks. It can't remove noise underneath your voice. If it swallows the tail of very quiet whispers, lower the threshold.
lim.p: Stops sudden loud sounds from clipping the output. There's no reason to turn it off.
out.p: The final level your apps receive. Pick a loudness target: the broadcast standard for call apps (−23 LUFS), or louder for recording and streaming (−16 LUFS). The slider is a fine trim.
h.try: Quick test: record and play back
try.note: Plays the same take twice, raw and then processed: the clearest way to hear whether your settings help. Unlike live monitoring, there's no latency.
mon.note.a: Call apps and browsers often apply their own noise suppression and auto gain; stacked on top of this chain, they degrade your voice. If your app's microphone is set to
mon.note.b: , turn off the app's own noise suppression.
mon.note2: Monitoring plays to your default output; use headphones only (on speakers the mic picks itself up and feeds back). Over Bluetooth headphones it lags by about a quarter second.
diag.hint: Tuning for mouth clicks, plosives and room noise needs real recordings of your voice. Six short takes are enough (about 1.5 minutes). Press “Guided recording”: each step appears in large text with a countdown, and missing or failed steps are recorded in order. Your settings don't change and nothing is played back.
diag.note: Recordings are unprocessed mic audio. They stay on this computer, in a folder only you can read, and are never sent anywhere.
diag.sentence: Pick up the pepper pot and tap it twice; tick, tock, knock on the door.
diag.sessiz.title: Room tone
diag.sessiz.prompt: Stay silent so the room tone can be recorded.
diag.aaa.title: Sustained vowel
diag.aaa.prompt: In your normal voice, hold a long “aaa” on one breath.
diag.ptk.title: Plosives
diag.fisilti.title: Whisper
diag.tik.title: Mouth clicks
diag.tik.prompt: Don't talk. Smack your lips or click your tongue once a second (5–6 times).
diag.metin.title: Read with pauses
diag.metin.prompt: In your normal voice, read “{sentence}” three times, pausing 2 seconds after each.
room.text: Room noise: {lufs} LUFS. Headroom above the silence threshold: {margins}.
room.bad: {modes} mode headroom is under {min} dB: the noise floor may rise while you're silent. Turn the mic's gain knob down a little or re-record somewhere quieter.
srv.busy: Another recording or playback is already running.
srv.diag_unreadable: Couldn't read the recording; try again.
srv.diag_silent: No signal from the mic (it may be muted on the device); try again.
srv.diag_clipped: The take clipped; back off from the mic a little and try again.
srv.diag_few_events: Picked up {events} clicks; at least {min} are needed. Make the lip smacks or tongue clicks a bit sharper and try again.
srv.diag_no_speech: No speech detected (the take is no louder than the room tone); follow the prompt and try again.
srv.diag_too_short: Too little speech ({sec} s); what was picked up may just be a bump or a tap. Follow the prompt from start to finish and try again.
srv.diag_choppy: The sound was broken up (longest unbroken stretch {sec} s); hold one steady “aaa” on a single breath. Try again.
srv.diag_busy_delete: Can't delete while a recording is running.
srv.chain_restarted: The chain restarted with the new layout; the mic will be back in a few seconds.
srv.live_restart_failed: Couldn't update the live chain: restart failed: {detail}
srv.pitch_missing: The pitch plugin isn't installed, so pitch can't be turned on. Install it with: bash tools/install_rubberband.sh
srv.monitor_during_trial: Monitoring can't be changed while a test is running.
srv.err_key: missing key: run `mic console` in a terminal and open the URL it prints
srv.err_name_rule: invalid name: use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (max 40)
srv.err_name_rule_char: invalid name: use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (max 40), and not a built-in character name
